extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers (study section members), and NIH staff involved in evaluating Research Project Grant (RPG) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and background on how NIH evaluates Research Project Grant (RPG) applications during the first stage of peer review, including the core scored review criteria and the role of additional/non-scored criteria in producing an Overall Impact score. Also describes high-level principles and the intent of the Simplified Review Framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of five scored criteria used to evaluate Research Project Grant (RPG) applications: Significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five scored criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, and Environment), along with several non-scored Additional Review Criteria, contribute to an application's final Overall Impact score. In current review practice (for applications with due dates before January 25, 2025), each of the five criteria is given a numerical score by assigned reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria (non-scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several non-scored Additional Review Criteria that also contribute to an application's Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references 'several non-scored Additional Review Criteria' but does not enumerate them in this excerpt. These non-scored criteria are considered along with the five scored criteria in forming the Overall Impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: An application's final Overall Impact score, to which the five scored criteria and the non-scored Additional Review Criteria contribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Overall Impact score is a key output of first-stage peer review and is used (along with second-level review and IC priorities) to inform funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of NIH peer review (fairness, independence, expertise, timeliness, freedom from inappropriate influences)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH seeks to ensure that applications receive fair, independent, expert, and timely scientific reviews—free from inappropriate influences—so NIH can fund the most promising research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles are foundational expectations for reviewers and the review process; NIH uses volunteer expert reviewers, conflict-of-interest management, and procedural safeguards to support these aims (contextual references to COI management and dual-level review are present elsewhere on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-level review and funding decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a rigorous dual-level peer review process: first-stage review for scientific and technical merit, followed by a second-level review by national advisory councils for mission relevance; final funding decisions are made by Institute/Center (IC) directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-stage review focuses on the five scored criteria and Additional Review Criteria to produce an Overall Impact score. Second-level review assesses mission relevance; IC directors then consider program priorities and existing portfolios when making final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Review Framework goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives of the Simplified Framework for NIH Peer Review: reduce complexity of the peer review process, reduce reviewer burdens related to policy compliance, and mitigate reputational bias so reviewers can focus on scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework was developed through CSR working groups, public input (including a Request for Information and consultations), and NIH-wide deliberation; implementation began in January 2025 with associated guidance and training resources for investigators, reviewers, and NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring practice timeframe note
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporal caveat on scoring practice: 'In current review practice (for applications with due dates before January 25, 2025), each of the five criteria is given a numerical score by assigned reviewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This note indicates that scoring procedures described applied to the pre-implementation period and that the Simplified Review Framework (implemented January 2025) may change or has changed specific scoring practices; users should consult latest reviewer guidance for current scoring details.
